name: Sonnet-Verdant
specific_features: Forests that emit harmonic resonances in wind
description: Sonnet-Verdant is a world of gentle beauty, its continents carpeted in vast deciduous forests interspersed with open grasslands that stretch toward distant mountain ranges. Twin river systems dominate the northern hemisphere, their tributaries carving deep canyons through sedimentary layers that reveal billions of years of geological history. The planet's axial tilt produces four distinct seasons, each painting the landscape in dramatically different palettes.

The atmosphere carries an unusual acoustic quality that early explorers found mesmerizing. Wind passing through the dominant tree species produces layered harmonic tones, creating an ever-shifting natural symphony that blankets entire continents. During the autumn months, bioluminescent organisms bloom across the meadowlands, turning the night side of the planet into a canvas of soft blue-green light visible from orbit.

Surveys suggest Sonnet-Verdant was once home to a pre-industrial civilization, though evidence is sparse and debated. Geometric stone arrangements dot the southern continent, too precise for natural formation yet too simple to confirm intelligent design. The planet's fauna shows unusual behavioral complexity, with several species demonstrating tool use and rudimentary communication, leading some xenobiologists to argue that intelligence is currently evolving here.

Colonial interests have been kept at bay by its designation as a protected biosphere, but pressure mounts as habitable worlds grow scarce. The harmonic forests alone represent a biological phenomenon found nowhere else in charted space. Whether the stone arrangements are evidence of a fallen civilization or merely geological curiosity, the planet's ecological richness makes it invaluable to science and dangerously attractive to exploitation.
